identified_issues: Violation of Section 8.4 operational prerequisites: direct block stream ingestion was initiated while 14 client write handles were active and dirty buffers were unverified.

Proxy-observation conflation: automated scanner treated valid RBAC permissions (CLUSTER_STORAGE_ADMIN) as sufficient evidence of safe operational execution, ignoring empirical telemetry of non-quiescent node state.
Critical risk of catastrophic journal desynchronization and unrecoverable data corruption due to overwriting underlying NVMe sectors during active client write transactions.
evidence: Node Supervisor Drain Log recorded 'Drain timeout after 8s: 14 client connections pinned by open write transactions. Drain aborted' at 2026-10-06T02:00:08.410Z.
Node state telemetry confirmed 'Node remains non-quiescent: 14 active client write handles connected' at 2026-10-06T02:00:08.420Z.

Block Synchronization Execution Log target check reported '14 active client handles; dirty buffers unverified' at 2026-10-06T02:00:15.050Z immediately prior to invoking CMD_SYNC_BLOCK_STREAM at 2026-10-06T02:00:15.100Z.
recommended_action: Reject the proposal to pass and clear the alert; immediately isolate STOR_NODE_06 from cluster traffic to assess file-system and transaction journal integrity, implement hard automated gating preventing CMD_SYNC_BLOCK_STREAM execution when active client handle count is non-zero, and require verification of quiescent dirty buffer flush before enabling low-level block synchronization.
